title: Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District, covering most of northern Wisconsin, is an open seat in 2026 after six-term Republican incumbent Tom Tiffany decided to run for governor rather than seek re-election. The district has been reliably Republican since former Rep. Sean Duffy flipped it in 2011, with Tiffany winning by margins of 24 to 27 points in his last two elections. Three Democrats and five Republicans are competing in the August 11 primary, with the Republican nominee expected to be heavily favored in the general election due to the district's strong conservative lean. Key issues in the race include rural economic development, healthcare access, and the constitutional role of Congress in checking executive power.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District race in the 2026 cycle as of mid-June 2026. The primary is still two months away, and general election polling has not yet been conducted.

candidates.name: Chris Armstrong
candidates.summary: Chris Armstrong is a first-time political candidate and small business owner from New Richmond, Wisconsin. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Astrophysics from the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Minnesota. Armstrong is running on a platform focused on defending the Constitution, addressing healthcare and housing costs, and rebuilding the rural economy.

candidates.name: Fred Clark
candidates.summary: Fred Clark is a former Wisconsin State Assembly member (2009–2015), a professional forester, conservation leader, and small business owner. He previously represented the Baraboo area and now lives in Bayfield, in the 7th District. Clark is running on a platform of rebuilding the rural economy, achieving universal healthcare, protecting the Constitution and rule of law, and responsible immigration and border policy.

candidates.name: Ginger Murray
candidates.summary: Ginger Murray is an attorney, small business owner, and former family court commissioner from New Lisbon, Wisconsin. A Northwoods native, she previously served as an attorney for the city of Crandon and town of Laona and ran for state legislature 26 years ago. Murray is running on a platform focused on education funding, economic stability for working families, healthcare access in rural areas, and environmental protection of the region's natural resources.

candidates.name: Michael Alfonso
candidates.summary: Michael Alfonso is a 26-year-old conservative activist and first-time candidate endorsed by President Donald Trump. He is the son-in-law of former 7th District U.S. Rep. Sean Duffy and holds a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Alfonso worked in construction and as a producer for The Dan Bongino Show, and is running on an America First platform emphasizing constitutional rights, economic freedom, and opposition to socialism.

candidates.name: Jessi Ebben
candidates.summary: Jessi Ebben is a Republican candidate and former congressional nominee who ran for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District in 2020, losing to Derrick Van Orden. A seventh-generation Wisconsinite, she describes herself as a Trump conservative focused on an America First agenda. Ebben was the first candidate to enter the 7th District race and has emphasized border security, economic nationalism, and conservative values.

candidates.name: Kevin Hermening
candidates.summary: Kevin Hermening is a Wausau businessman, former Marathon County Republican Party chairman, and former Mosinee School Board member. He is running as a conservative Republican emphasizing his local roots in the district and experience in public service. Hermening has criticized out-of-district candidates as 'carpetbaggers' and stresses his consistent voting record within the 7th District.

candidates.name: Niina Threlfall-Baum
candidates.summary: Niina Threlfall-Baum is a Republican candidate who was raised on a Wisconsin dairy farm and describes herself as a principles-first, independent-minded moderate. She was the first candidate in the 7th District race to secure ballot access. Threlfall-Baum is running without corporate PAC funding and emphasizes a pragmatic approach to governance.

candidates.name: Donald Raihala
candidates.summary: Donald 'Don' Raihala is an accountant and perennial candidate who filed nomination papers in June 2026 for his fourth run for the U.S. House in Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District. He entered the race late, after other candidates had already announced, and is running as a Republican.
